title: Constructible devissage: the thick-subcategory generation
statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type scheme over $k$ and $A$ a
finite coefficient ring as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions].
The triangulated category $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ is the thick subcategory of
$D(X,A)$ generated by the objects

$$
Rg_*j_!L ,
$$

where $U$ is a locally closed stratum of $X$,
$j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ is the open immersion into its closure,
$g:\overline U\hookrightarrow X$ is the closed immersion, and $L$ is a lisse
sheaf of $A$-modules on $U$ with flat stalks. Constant coefficients
$L=A_U$ do not suffice in general.

proof.text: The finite coefficient ring A=O_E/(varpi_E)^n is annihilated by l^n. Indeed spectralNorm_extends and the p-adic norm of l show |l|_E<1. The maximal ideal membership clause of Padic.extension_integers_dvr therefore puts l in m_E. The same theorem identifies the ideal generated by the chosen uniformizer with m_E; hence l^n is in m_E^n, the defining coefficient ideal. The quotient map kills l^n, and n is positive by the coefficient convention.

source.place: Proof Steps 0–2, finite coefficient hypothesis for the flat-model generation theorem

proof.text: Equip X with its given structure morphism over Spec k and specialize proEtaleThickGeneration_eq of [sk-lem-sf-flat-model] to A, using its finite coefficient-ring instance and the preceding annihilation. Its closure generators are definitionally sfProEtaleClosureGenerators, with the actual scheme-theoretic closure factorization. The only remaining difference is boundedness: a finite set of nonzero cohomology degrees has integer lower and upper bounds, while the degrees between any two integer bounds form a finite set. Reassociate the constructibility, boundedness and finite-Tor conjunctions. This proves the generation equality without repeating the flat-model, filtration and comparison proof of the existing theorem.

source.place: First paragraph, generation clause, already formalized as proEtaleThickGeneration_eq

proof.text: For the comparison part, put $\mathcal A=D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ and $\mathcal B=D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Proet},A)$. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives an equivalence on bounded constructible categories. The two directions of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] restrict it to $E=\nu_X^*:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal B$, preserving each Tor interval: a bounded constructible preimage is bounded below, as required in direction (ii). Here $\ell$ is invertible since $X$ is over $k$ and $\ell\ne p$. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], $E$ is exact with its termwise shift comparison. The inverse is exact with the induced shift comparisons by [lem-trf-exact-equivalence-inverse].

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: transport of immersion generators to the pro-étale convention

proof.text: For a closed immersion $g:\overline U\hookrightarrow X$, [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives $g^{-1}(\Spec R)=\Spec(R/I)$, so $g$ is quasi-compact. It is a monomorphism: maps through the quotient on affine charts are unique. Hence its diagonal is an isomorphism and is quasi-compact, so $g$ is quasi-separated. This checks the geometric hypotheses of the direct-image comparison used next.

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: transport of immersion generators to the pro-étale convention

proof.text:
Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to $g$ and the degree-zero sheaf $j^{\Et}_!L$ (thus a bounded-below complex), and then [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] to the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$. Their composite is the natural isomorphism
$$E(Rg_{\Et,*}j^{\Et}_!L)\cong Rg_{\Proet,*}\nu_{\overline U}^*j^{\Et}_!L\cong Rg_{\Proet,*}j^{\Proet}_!\nu_U^*L.$$
These are the actual immersion generators on the two sites, with the same $j$ and $g$.

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: transport of immersion generators to the pro-étale convention

proof.text: The image family exhausts the allowed pro-etale generators up to isomorphism. Indeed [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] both sends etale lisse sheaves to pro-etale lisse sheaves and descends every finite-stalk pro-etale lisse sheaf to an etale lisse sheaf. The $A$-linear stalk isomorphism of [lem-cbc-proetale-comparison-stalk] preserves flatness of these stalks in both directions. Consequently Step 5 matches the full generator families. For the constant subfamilies, clause (1) of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] gives $\nu_U^*A_U\cong A_U$, so Step 5 also matches every constant generator.

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: transport of immersion generators to the pro-étale convention

proof.text: For the still-unproved constant-coefficient clause, use [sk-lem-sf-flat-model] for thickness and generation of the etale and pro-etale finite-Tor constructible categories inside their ambient derived categories. Apply [lem-trf-ambient-thick-closure-equivalence] to these subcategories and the exact comparison equivalence of Step 3. Steps 5–6 identify the immersion generator families. In particular, applying the same lemma to the constant subfamily preserves and reflects membership in its ambient thick closure. This is the transport used by the counterexample in Steps 8–10; it is not needed again for the already-proved generation equality.

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: transport of immersion generators to the pro-étale convention

proof.text: For the constant-coefficient obstruction take $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_5$, $X=\mathbf G_m=\Spec k[t,t^{-1}]$ and $A=\mathbf F_3$ (the coefficient datum $\ell=3$, $E=\mathbf Q_3$, $n=1$). Consider the double cover $\pi:V=\Spec k[u,u^{-1}]\to X$, $t=u^2$. Its algebra is free of rank two with basis $1,u$, and it is étale by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] applied to $Q(T)=T^2-t$, since $Q'=2u$ is invertible. The fibre of $\pi$ at a geometric generic point has two elements. By [thm-galois-fundamental] its permutation action gives a continuous character $\chi:\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)\to S_2\cong\{1,-1\}\subset\mathbf F_3^\times$. The finite-coefficient equivalence of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] realizes the one-dimensional sign representation as a lisse sheaf $L$ on $X$. Its local model is the free module $\mathbf F_3$, so $L$ is an allowed flat generator and belongs to $D^b_{ctf}$ by the generation result of Step 2 with $j=g=1_X$.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: construction of the order-two Kummer local system

proof.text: Let $h:\eta=\Spec k(t)\to X$ be the generic-point map. Its exact inverse image on module sheaves is [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so it induces a triangulated functor by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Use the exact equivalence [lem-exc-field-discrete-modules] to view its values as complexes of discrete $A[G]$-modules, $G=\operatorname{Gal}(k(t)^{\mathrm{sep}}/k(t))$. Define $\mathcal T$ to consist of complexes whose resulting cohomology is zero outside finitely many degrees and in each degree has a finite filtration with trivial one-dimensional $G$-quotients. This is a thick subcategory of the ambient derived category. Indeed intersection with a submodule and passage to the images of a filtration prove the submodule and quotient assertions (a subquotient of a trivial one-dimensional module is zero or that module); inverse images of a quotient's filtration concatenate with a submodule's filtration to prove closure under extensions. The long exact cohomology sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] then proves closure under triangles, since each middle cohomology is an extension of a quotient and a submodule of the adjacent cohomologies. The degree bound is the finite union of the two bounds with a shift. Shifts reindex the filtrations, and a retract gives a submodule on every cohomology group, proving closure under direct summands.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: the thick obstruction, with the filtration argument supplied

proof.text: Every constant-coefficient generator $Rg_*j_!A_U$ lies in $\mathcal T$. If its stratum omits $\eta$, its generic stalk is zero by the finite stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] for the closed immersion, which is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], and the vanishing assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks]. If its stratum contains $\eta$, that locally closed subset is open dense in the integral $X$, its closure is $X$, and its restriction to $\eta$ is the constant $A$ with trivial $G$-action; these identifications are natural in the geometric point and hence $G$-equivariant. The derived generator is a sheaf by [lem-fin-closed-immersion]. Thus the thick closure of all constant-coefficient generators lies in $\mathcal T$. In contrast $h^*L$ is the nontrivial one-dimensional sign representation. To verify nontriviality, $t$ is not a square in $k(t)$: an equality $f(t)^2=tg(t)^2$ with coprime polynomials forces $t\mid f$ and then $t\mid g$, a contradiction. Hence $k(t)[u]/(u^2-t)$ is a separable quadratic field extension. By [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification] its two-element geometric fibre is a transitive $G$-set, so some element swaps the roots. Base-change compatibility in [thm-galois-fundamental] identifies this action with the restriction of $\chi$, giving the scalar $-1\ne1$ on $h^*L$. A one-dimensional nontrivial representation cannot have a filtration with trivial quotients. Therefore $L\notin\mathcal T$, and constant-coefficient generators do not generate $D^b_{ctf}$. Finally Steps 3–7 transport both the constant generators and $L$ across the comparison equivalence, so the same failure holds in the pro-étale convention of the item.
